facebook.note: Page exists per task brief but is login-walled; content could not be extracted or independently confirmed to be the correct/current page in this session. Per instructions, NOT included in JSON-LD sameAs and NOT linked anywhere on the site to avoid pointing users to an unverified URL. Recorded here only for the internal record.

booking_platform: None. Phone/text only, no online booking platform of any kind (no Booksy/Square/GlossGenius/Vagaro/Mangomint/Fresha presence found).
rating_source: Google, surfaced via DogDog.org, a pet-groomer directory whose page for this business embeds a live Google Maps iframe keyed to Google Place ID ChIJW68b7RZZ7IgRznzI1vXZDDk and shows an aria-label reading 'Rating: 4.5 out of 5, 64 people rated this' alongside a Google-CDN-hosted business photo. This session's own WebFetch of the DogDog.org page (2026-07-23) independently re-confirmed the address, phone and the '64 people rated this' figure live (star value itself was not rendered as plain text in the fetched markdown, but the count and place linkage matched exactly). Treated as rating_source: 'Google (via place-ID-linked directory DogDog.org)', i.e. a Google rating surfaced through a third-party directory rather than scraped directly from Google Maps/Business Profile. A corroborating Yelp rating also shows 4.5 stars with 16-17 reviews (yelp.com/biz/angels-have-paws-pet-grooming-salon-tallahassee, per task brief; direct WebFetch of the Yelp page returned HTTP 403 in this session, consistent with Yelp's known bot-blocking, so this session relied on the task brief's citation rather than re-fetching it). The site and JSON-LD use the Google/DogDog.org figure (4.5 / 64) as the headline stat since it is the larger, place-ID-anchored sample; Yelp is cited separately on-site (gallery CTA 'See on Yelp', footer 'Yelp · 4.5 stars') as a secondary corroborating source, clearly labeled as Yelp and not conflated with the Google number. Note: a WebSearch AI-overview summary surfaced a third figure ('4.6 stars, 73 reviews', OurPetGroomer.com) which was NOT used, since it could not be traced to a primary source and conflicts with both the Google/DogDog.org and Yelp figures; flagged here for transparency rather than silently discarded.

hours.note: By appointment only, no walk-ins. Source: PawPartner.com listing (per task brief), independently re-confirmed live in this session via WebFetch of the DogDog.org page, which lists the identical 'Monday - Friday: 7 AM to 6 PM, Saturday - Sunday: Closed' schedule.

services_source: Task brief research (full-service salon: bathing, haircuts, ear cleaning, nail trimming, paw treatments, teeth cleaning; species dogs/cats/rabbits/rodents/birds). Independently re-confirmed live in this session via WebSearch/WebFetch of ourpetgroomer.com and dogdog.org, which list an identical service set. services_menu.pricing: Not published anywhere. Site renders services without invented prices and uses a 'Call for pricing' / 'Precio por consulta' note throughout, following the precedent set by output/oddjobrob (services rendered without prices when none are published).

images.curation_note: All 5 Nextdoor photos and the logo were used exactly as instructed. nextdoor-post-02 shows a recognizable staff member; per general pipeline gallery-curation guidance (no owner/staff portraits as gallery tiles) it would normally go to the experience/about section only, but the task brief explicitly enumerated all 5 files for gallery tiles with a matching example caption ('Front Desk'), so it was used in both the experience section and the gallery, consistent with the brief's explicit instruction and with how small photo pools are handled elsewhere in this pipeline (image reuse across sections, see output/divine-elegance-studio-wpb/data.json).

brand_vibe: Purple/lavender accent wall with warm wood-tone cabinetry in the real salon photos; playful 'Dogs Welcome People Tolerated' signage; real logo is a rich amethyst purple (#730c99 sampled directly from the logo file) paw-and-pet mark with a teal 'PET SALON' wordmark accent. Base kept LIGHT/warm cream per brand brief, with a fresh amethyst/orchid accent distinct from the project's existing 'violeta dark #b18ae8' palette (see DESIGN.md 'Paletas ya usadas').
base_template: templates/light-v2 (light base, lashbloom exemplar, EN default)

palette.derivation: accent_deep sampled directly (PIL pixel sampling, most common non-white pixel color in the wordmark region) from assets/raw/logo-angels-have-paws.jpg = #730c99 (amethyst/orchid). accent_mid, bg, bg-2, ink and all supporting gradient/shadow/orb tones were computed programmatically (lighten/darken/mix against #730c99 and #9a50b6) to keep the whole palette internally consistent, distinct from the project's already-used 'violeta dark #b18ae8' and from every other listed palette in DESIGN.md.

jsonld_type_note: Used @type: LocalBusiness. schema.org has no formally valid 'PetGroomingService' type (checked before deciding), so LocalBusiness was used as the safe, always-valid choice per the task brief's fallback instruction ('LocalBusiness or PetGroomingService if valid schema.org type').
build_method: Anchored transformation script (Python, rep()/rep_all() with assert-before-replace) over templates/light-v2/index.html per templates/SKELETONS-V2.md, run as 12 sequential staged scripts (palette hex+rgba global replace, head/meta/JSON-LD, nav+preloader, hero, strip+marquee, experience, method/steps, services grid+full categorized menu, gallery grid, reviews, location, CTA+footer+book-float). index.html was never written from scratch.
